prOriginal.nota: Found via gh api commits/<head>/pulls; PR headRefOid equals the benchmark head 5b229316ee, merged as-is (commit is an ancestor of main). Reverted in full the same day by Jeff Atwood (2b2ae4bfe7).

optimize-header-layout-performance-with-.reason: The flex container on .d-header .contents and the flex-item rules on .extra-info-wrapper were introduced by PR #3641 and removed the same day by commit 2b2ae4bfe7, an exact revert of 5b229316ee across all 5 files. The header returned to the float layout, so the long-title overflow caused by the flex item never persisted. Later flexbox attempts (PR #3732, closed unmerged; 2016 widget header rewrite) are separate code. Reclassified as descontinuado for consistency: a whole-PR revert with no stated reason does not target this bug (same rule as the other reverted PRs).

astra.pergunta: PR #3641 was merged 2015-08-04 and fully reverted by Jeff Atwood ~1.5h later (commit 2b2ae4bfe7, no reason stated). Does an unexplained full revert count as confirmado or descontinuado for #01, #02, #05?
astra.resposta: All three confirmado: the revert undid the flex layout (#01), removed the defective mixin and its uses (#02) and restored float:right (#05). Under 'any way of fixing counts', a full rollback of the introducing change is a fix; the missing justification only means upstream did not acknowledge each bug.
